name: Meadows Row
summary: A single-arm landmine row, named after John Meadows, performed side-on to the bar for a deep stretch and strong contraction in the lats and mid back.
setup: Anchor a barbell in a landmine or corner and load the free end.
Stand perpendicular to the bar, hinge at the hips and grip the thick end of the bar near the plates with an overhand grip.
Rest your free hand on your thigh or a support to stay stable with a flat back.
execution: Pull the elbow up and back toward your hip.
Squeeze the shoulder blade toward the spine at the top.
Lower until the arm is straight, allowing a stretch at the bottom.
Finish all reps, then switch sides.
mistakes: Rotating the torso: use less load and brace the abs.
Rounding the back: keep a long spine and a proud chest.
Using only the biceps: lead with the elbow.
Pulling too high toward the shoulder: pull toward the hip.
